topic: Sharp identifying-degree frontier for rationally identifiable acyclic linear Gaussian mixed graphs with directed indegree at most two. Let ID_G be the source-defined minimum, over recursive identifying orders, of the largest total polynomial degree in any certificate, and let D2(n) maximize ID_G over identifiable n-vertex graphs. Prove matching asymptotic upper and lower bounds for D2(n), including an explicit graph family whose degree cannot be reduced by recursive substitutions through structural or error parameters; compile the upper bound into a total stopping schedule for DegBoundedIdentifiability; and give plug-in influence-function and simultaneous Wald inference for the returned rational formulas on fixed denominator, covariance-eigenvalue, and nondegeneracy charts. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Exact rank-intersection closure over all original parameters was derived and used to enumerate all 64 topologically labelled three-vertex mixed graphs, yielding D2(3)=3: eight degree-one, twenty-one degree-two, two degree-three, and thirty-three generically rank-deficient graphs. A positive-definite six-vertex directed chain outside HTC was constructed; two quadratic cycle equations with distinct second roots cancel to give a rational certificate of degree at most nine. Checks covered bow nonidentification, cycle ambiguity, error-parameter shortcuts, generic-elimination collapse, and current tree-identification work; no exact frontier collision was found. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Determine the sharp graph-uniform closure degree for every rationally identifiable indegree-two graph and construct a matching family whose degree-d closure remains proper below that threshold. EARLY KILL TEST: Compute exact degree-four closure for the six-vertex two-triangle graph, including error parameters; if it is complete, abandon cycle length as growth evidence and test constant-degree completeness before enlarging the family. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/eid_indegree2_formula_degree.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the sharp asymptotic growth of the minimum recursive certificate degree D2(n) for rationally identifiable acyclic linear Gaussian mixed graphs of directed indegree at most two, including an explicit family whose degree lower bound survives substitutions through all previously identified structural and error parameters.

source_refs.claim: The degree-bounded algorithm finds a lowest-degree identifying formula only after a maximal degree d is supplied; it does not give a graph-uniform degree frontier.
source_refs.author: Benjamin Hollering, Pratik Misra, Nils Sturma

source_refs.claim: HTC gives polynomial-time rational identification by recursively solving generically invertible linear systems, while exhaustive algebraic calculations expose identifiable graphs outside the criterion.
source_refs.author: Rina Foygel, Jan Draisma, Mathias Drton

source_refs.claim: For tree-directed models, missing bidirected-edge cycles generate quadratic systems whose distinct roots can sometimes be combined to recover a unique rational solution.
source_refs.author: Benito van der Zander, Marcel Wienöbst, Markus Bläser, Maciej Liśkiewicz

open_problems.why_unsolved: The existing strands control different objects: HTC controls recursive linear systems, tree-identification papers control local bilinear or quadratic missing-cycle equations when every node has one directed parent, and Hollering–Misra–Sturma search optimally only below an externally supplied degree. None supplies an invariant bounding the degree of the birational inverse of the covariance parametrization under indegree two. A lower bound is especially nontrivial because a high-degree elimination polynomial in one presentation can collapse after a different recursive order or after substitution of an identified error covariance, so resultant degree alone is not intrinsic.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem giving an explicit function f(n) and constants c,C with c f(n) ≤ D2(n) ≤ C f(n), together with graphs G_n and a coordinate-ring, filtration, or birational-inverse argument proving that every allowed recursive certificate for G_n has degree at least c f(n).

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves directly from complete but impractical Gröbner elimination to degree-bounded symbolic identification, which is the natural narrative for asking how large the degree parameter must be.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Complete symbolic identification is doubly exponential -> bounded-degree search is quasi-polynomial and returns minimum-degree formulas -> its degree input has no known graph-uniform calibration -> determine the sharp indegree-two degree frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate missing bidirected edges into bilinear equations, solve cycle systems through resultants, and use extra cycles to eliminate spurious quadratic roots.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest existing mechanism by which locally quadratic certificates combine into a rational formula; an indegree-two lower-bound family must show where this elimination grows in degree and cannot be shortcut.

method_exemplars.technique: Bound degrees of inverse birational maps using the graph of the map, its base ideal, Rees algebra, and regularity under a Cohen–Macaulay hypothesis.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The covariance parametrization of an identifiable mixed graph is generically birational onto its image, so inverse-map degree machinery is suited to an intrinsic bound invariant to recursive substitutions.

method_exemplars.technique: Differentiate a recursively defined identifying system, propagate earlier-stage influence functions, and estimate the resulting joint sandwich covariance from observable moments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once the frontier theorem returns rational structural coefficients, this supplies the closest existing inference proof for recursively identified linear-SEM parameters.

open_problems.open_problem: Extend the complete missing-cycle classification for tree-directed mixed graphs to acyclic directed-indegree-two graphs by deciding whether recursive closure at an absolute constant degree is complete or whether interacting two-parent gadgets force unbounded certificate degree.

source_refs.claim: Tree-directed mixed graphs admit a complete randomized polynomial-time classification into identifiable, two-identifiable, and unidentifiable parameters using missing-edge components and identifying cycles.
source_refs.author: Aaryan Gupta, Markus Bläser

source_refs.claim: TreeID shows that missing cycles yield quadratic equations and that multiple cycles can select a unique rational root, but the original algorithm was not proved complete.
source_refs.author: Benito van der Zander, Marcel Wienöbst, Markus Bläser, Maciej Liśkiewicz

source_refs.claim: The complete tree-directed identification algorithm can be accelerated to O(n^3 log^2 n), but the result remains confined to directed trees.
source_refs.author: Yasmine Briefs, Markus Bläser

open_problems.why_unsolved: The completeness proof for directed trees uses the fact that each missing-edge equation contains the two parameters attached to unique incoming directed edges, reducing connected components to plane bilinear systems of rank one or two. With two parents, a missing covariance equation can retain several unresolved structural coefficients and error parameters; the component propagation and common-square-root representation used in the tree proof no longer close. The literature scan found no extension of that classification or constant-degree closure theorem for directed indegree two.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either a complete graphical-algebraic classification proving that every rationally identifiable indegree-two graph is resolved by recursive certificates of degree at most a universal constant c, or an explicit indegree-two graph sequence with a theorem that its required closure degree diverges.

writing_exemplar.why: Its formulation isolates a sharply restricted graph class, explains why general Gröbner methods are excessive, and asks for a complete structural classification.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: General mixed-graph identification is incomplete or expensive -> a directed-tree restriction exposes tractable missing-cycle structure -> tree parameters have a complete one/two/infinite-fiber classification -> test whether the first non-tree case, indegree two, retains bounded-degree completeness.

method_exemplars.technique: Decompose the missing-edge graph into low-rank components, detect identifying cycles through randomized polynomial identity tests, and propagate the resulting FASTP solutions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: An indegree-two theorem must replace the first proof step that fails—the reduction of each component to two-variable bilinear equations—while retaining a completeness argument.

method_exemplars.technique: Compute adaptive degree-bounded Gröbner information and extract a lowest-degree rational identification formula.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It can certify candidate constant-degree closures on finite test families and supplies the algebraic target against which a new graphical closure theorem must be proved.

method_exemplars.technique: Obtain influence functions by differentiating recursive identification equations and accounting for uncertainty from earlier identified coefficients.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Any new recursive indegree-two closure admits an estimation rung if its nonlinear step is differentiated in addition to the established recursive corrections.

open_problems.open_problem: Compile a graph-uniform degree bound for rationally identifiable acyclic indegree-two mixed graphs into a total stopping schedule for degree-bounded identification, with explicit end-to-end time and space bounds and correctness for every graph in the class.

source_refs.claim: The symbolic algorithm is complete only relative to a prespecified maximal formula degree d and has quasi-polynomial complexity below that bound.
source_refs.author: Benjamin Hollering, Pratik Misra, Nils Sturma

source_refs.claim: Generic identification in unrestricted linear SCMs has a sound and complete polynomial-space algorithm, while instance-level fiber-cardinality questions are coNP-hard and hard for the co-class of the existential theory of the reals.
source_refs.author: Julian Dörfler, Benito van der Zander, Markus Bläser, Maciej Liśkiewicz

source_refs.claim: Some stronger graphical identification searches are NP-complete, while instrumental cutsets provide a polynomial-time sufficient criterion for acyclic linear SCMs.
source_refs.author: Daniel Kumor, Bryant Chen, Elias Bareinboim

open_problems.why_unsolved: Degree-bounded identification is presently a promise procedure: failure at degree d says only that no formula of degree at most d exists. The general polynomial-space decision algorithm addresses generic fiber cardinality rather than furnishing a low-degree rational inverse, and general hardness results do not calibrate the indegree-two class. A finite schedule therefore needs a structural cap B(n), proof that every rationally identifiable coefficient is encountered by that cap under adaptive ordering, and substitution of B(n) into the symbolic complexity bound.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem specifying B(n), a schedule invoking degree-bounded identification through degree B(n), and proofs of termination, soundness, formula completeness for every rationally identifiable indegree-two graph, and explicit runtime and memory bounds in n and B(n).

writing_exemplar.why: Its algorithm-and-complexity presentation is the direct model for explaining why a structural degree theorem converts bounded search into a total procedure.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Gröbner completeness is computationally prohibitive -> adaptive bounded-degree search is efficient and formula-producing -> bounded search lacks a principled stopping degree -> an indegree-two degree cap yields a total scheduled algorithm.

method_exemplars.technique: Use weighted homogenization, adaptive variable orderings, and degree-truncated Gröbner computation to recover the minimum-degree rational formula below a supplied bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired stopping theorem compiles a structural cap into this algorithm, so its completeness and complexity lemmas are the proof interface.

method_exemplars.technique: Decide generic identification with a sound and complete polynomial-space algebraic procedure and analyze the relevant real-algebraic decision complexity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the closest total-algorithm benchmark and clarifies which decision guarantees must be distinguished from rational formula recovery.

method_exemplars.technique: Turn a recursive rational identification procedure into a computable estimator and influence-function covariance recursion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A formula-returning total algorithm has a natural downstream statistical contract, and this is the closest worked compilation from graph algorithm to inference.

open_problems.open_problem: Develop plug-in influence functions, a joint limit law, and simultaneous Wald inference for an arbitrary finite vector of rational structural-coefficient formulas returned by degree-bounded identification on charts with denominators, covariance eigenvalues, and derivative nondegeneracy bounded away from zero.

source_refs.claim: Influence functions and asymptotic normality are derived for HTC estimators with fixed witness sets, yielding confidence regions and Wald tests for structural coefficients.
source_refs.author: Leopold Mareis, Nils Sturma, Mathias Drton

source_refs.claim: Degree-bounded symbolic identification returns general lowest-degree rational formulas, but its contribution is identification and symbolic complexity rather than sampling inference.
source_refs.author: Benjamin Hollering, Pratik Misra, Nils Sturma

source_refs.claim: When a tested polynomial constraint has vanishing gradient, ordinary Wald limits can become nonstandard rational functions of Gaussian variables.
source_refs.author: Mathias Drton, Han Xiao

open_problems.why_unsolved: HTC inference exploits the special representation beta_v=A_v^{-1}b_v and recursively corrects fixed earlier-stage estimates. A degree-bounded output may instead be an arbitrary quotient of multivariate covariance polynomials, may share denominators across coefficients, and may be selected from multiple formulas or recursive orders. Validity requires proving chartwise differentiability, consistent evaluation of the full cross-covariance, and regularity of the Wald map; Drton–Xiao shows that derivative degeneracy changes the limiting law and cannot be ignored.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: For theta=f(vech Sigma) with rational coordinates returned by the algorithm, a theorem giving the observable influence vector Df_Sigma[vech(XX^T-Sigma)], a consistent plug-in covariance estimator, joint asymptotic normality uniformly on fixed regular charts, and simultaneous ellipsoidal or max-t Wald confidence sets with stated coverage.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames the gap between a closed-form identification algorithm and an inferentially usable estimator, then develops the influence-function object before confidence regions and Wald tests.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Graphical identification yields closed-form causal coefficients -> formulas alone do not provide uncertainty quantification -> HTC formulas now have recursive influence-function theory -> arbitrary rational formulas returned by symbolic identification need joint chartwise inference.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply the functional delta method to identification equations, retain earlier-stage correction terms, and reduce the sandwich variance to observable fourth moments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target is the same vector of structural causal coefficients from a covariance matrix; only the identification map changes from recursive linear solves to general rational functions.

method_exemplars.technique: Analyze Wald statistics through the leading homogeneous Taylor term when the first derivative vanishes, producing nonstandard rational-Gaussian limits.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It identifies why derivative nondegeneracy is load-bearing and supplies the counter-regime outside the proposed regular chart.

method_exemplars.technique: Control perturbation of recovered linear-SEM parameters through condition-number analysis and exhibit small graphs with unbounded inverse sensitivity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Uniform plug-in inference for rational inverse maps requires the same local conditioning control in addition to pointwise differentiability.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the additional conditioning restrictions, beyond positive covariance eigenvalues and nonzero rational denominators, that are sufficient and close to necessary for uniform finite-sample concentration and Wald coverage of degree-bounded rational identification formulas.

source_refs.claim: Bow-free LSEM recovery is stable under a sufficient condition, but a four-vertex LSEM can have unbounded recovery condition number.
source_refs.author: Karthik Abinav Sankararaman, Anand Louis, Navin Goyal

source_refs.claim: The symbolic procedure minimizes algebraic formula degree, an objective that does not itself bound numerical sensitivity of the resulting rational inverse.
source_refs.author: Benjamin Hollering, Pratik Misra, Nils Sturma

source_refs.claim: For HTC estimators, asymptotic variance depends substantially on the valid witness-set choice even when every choice identifies the same coefficient.
source_refs.author: Leopold Mareis, Nils Sturma, Mathias Drton

open_problems.why_unsolved: A denominator lower bound prevents poles of one displayed quotient, and a covariance-eigenvalue lower bound avoids singular observational laws, but neither automatically bounds the derivative of the inverse parametrization or the coefficients and gradients of high-degree numerator and denominator polynomials. The four-node instability example shows that generic identifiability can coexist with arbitrarily poor conditioning, while witness-dependent HTC variances show that algebraically valid formulas can differ sharply in statistical behavior. What is missing is a chart stated in intrinsic inverse-map terms and a proof relating that chart to formula-level quantities available from symbolic output.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp sufficient-condition theorem bounding the Jacobian or condition number of each returned causal functional on an explicit regular chart, together with a finite-sample simultaneous concentration or coverage bound and a counterexample showing failure when an essential chart condition is removed.

writing_exemplar.why: It separates algebraic identifiability from numerical reliability and motivates stability through finite-sample perturbation of the observational covariance.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Generic identification establishes a formal inverse -> empirical covariance perturbs the inverse's input -> some identifiable models are arbitrarily ill-conditioned -> characterize regular charts that make high-degree rational recovery statistically stable.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive inverse-problem condition numbers from matrix perturbation inequalities and construct explicit parameter sequences exhibiting unbounded sensitivity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested result is a condition-number theorem for a broader rational inverse class, with the same need for both a stable region and a sharp failure example.

method_exemplars.technique: Return reduced minimum-degree rational formulas through adaptive symbolic elimination.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Those numerator-denominator pairs are the concrete objects whose derivatives and coefficient growth must be related to intrinsic inverse conditioning.

method_exemplars.technique: Express estimator variance through the influence function and compare statistically distinct valid identification choices.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the variance-side diagnostic needed to connect symbolic formula choice and chart conditioning to attainable coverage.

literature_map:
Sullivant–Talaska–Draisma (2010, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:0812.1938) characterize covariance-submatrix ranks by trek separation and determinant expansions.
Drton–Foygel–Sullivant (2011, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1003.1146) give a graph-theoretic characterization of global injectivity, distinct from generic rational recovery.
Foygel–Draisma–Drton (2012, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1107.5552) introduce HTC: polynomial-time sufficient rational identification by recursive linear systems, with a documented sufficient/necessary gap.
Drton–Weihs (2016, Scandinavian Journal of Statistics, DOI:10.1111/sjos.12227) enlarge HTC reach by ancestral decomposition; Chen (2016, NeurIPS) adds edge-set identification and recursive decomposition.
Weihs et al. (2018, Journal of Causal Inference, arXiv:1702.03884) recover individual edges as quotients of covariance subdeterminants, linking trek systems to explicit low-degree formulas.
Yao–Evans (2022, Algebraic Statistics, arXiv:1911.12754) characterize HTC identification through specified linear-algebra operations and generate model ideals for HTC graphs.
Van der Zander et al. (2022, AISTATS, arXiv:2203.01852) show that missing cycles in tree-directed models yield quadratic systems and that extra cycles can remove a second root.
Gupta–Bläser (2024, AAAI, arXiv:2311.14058) make the tree-directed classification complete and polynomial-time; Briefs–Bläser (2025, NeurIPS) improve its runtime to O(n^3 log^2 n).
Kumor–Chen–Bareinboim (2019, NeurIPS) show hardness for stronger graphical searches and provide efficient instrumental cutsets, emphasizing the gap between useful criteria and completeness.
Dörfler et al. (2024, NeurIPS, arXiv:2407.12528) give a complete polynomial-space generic-identification algorithm and hardness results for identification-related fiber questions.
Barber–Drton–Sturma–Weihs (2022, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:2201.04457) extend half-trek reasoning to latent-factor models and still obtain rational formulas through bounded combinatorial searches.
Hollering–Misra–Sturma (2026, arXiv:2604.20516) find lowest-degree rational formulas quasi-polynomially below a user-supplied degree d; no located result supplies d as a function of n or directed indegree.
Sankararaman–Louis–Goyal (2020, UAI, arXiv:1905.06836) separate identifiability from stability, proving stable bow-free regimes but also a four-node example with unbounded condition number.
Mareis–Sturma–Drton (2026, arXiv:2606.26931) derive recursive influence functions and Wald inference for fixed HTC estimators; the scan found no corresponding theory for arbitrary symbolic rational formulas or adaptive formula choice.
Across these papers, the unoccupied junction is an intrinsic formula-degree frontier for acyclic indegree-two mixed graphs, a resulting total degree schedule, and statistically regular inference for the formulas that schedule returns.
